lines.name: Alola Geodude → Alola Graveler → Alola Golem
Mime Jr. → Galar Mr. Mime → Mr. Rime

flavor.3: A bewitching aroma wafts from its flower. The fragrance becalms those engaged in a battle.
flavor.6: Its wings can carry this Pokémon close to an altitude of 4,600 feet. It blows out fire at very high temperatures.
flavor.9: The rocket cannons on its shell fire jets of water capable of punching holes through thick steel.
flavor.12: It collects honey every day. It rubs honey onto the hairs on its legs to carry it back to its nest.
flavor.15: It has three poisonous stingers on its forelegs and its tail. They are used to jab its enemy repeatedly.
flavor.18: This Pokémon flies at Mach 2 speed, seeking prey. Its large talons are feared as wicked weapons.
flavor.20: Its hind feet are webbed. They act as flippers, so it can swim in rivers and hunt for prey.
flavor.22: A Pokémon that dates back many years. If it senses danger, it flies high and away, instantly.
flavor.24: The frightening patterns on its belly have been studied. Six variations have been confirmed.
flavor.28: It climbs trees by hooking on with its sharp claws. Sandslash shares the berries it gathers, dropping them down to Sandshrew waiting below the tree.
flavor.31: It pacifies offspring by placing them in the gaps between the spines on its back. The spines will never secrete poison while young are present.
flavor.34: Nidoking prides itself on its strength. It’s forceful and spirited in battle, making use of its thick tail and diamond-crushing horn.
flavor.38: The coat of gleaming golden fur is quite magnificent. This species is said to store sacred power in its nine long tails and to live for a millennium.
flavor.169: Its hind limbs have become another set of wings. Crobat expertly maneuvers its four wings to dart in exquisite fashion through even the most confined caves without losing any speed.
flavor.45: The larger its petals, the more toxic pollen it contains. Its big head is heavy and hard to hold up.
flavor.182: Bellossom gather at times and appear to dance. They say that the dance is a ritual to summon the sun.
flavor.47: Mushroom-lacking specimens of this Pokémon lie unmoving in the forest, lending credence to the hypothesis that the large mushroom is in control of Parasect's actions.
flavor.49: The powdery scales on its wings are hard to remove from skin. They also contain poison that leaks out on contact.
flavor.51: These Diglett triplets dig over 60 miles below sea level. No one knows what it’s like underground.
flavor.53: Its elegant and refined behavior clashes with that of the barbaric Perrserker. The relationship between the two is one of mutual disdain.
flavor.55: Its body is strong, and it has webbing on its hands and feet. Golduck can swim easily through rough seas, clawing its way through the high waves.
flavor.979: It imbues its fists with the power of the rage that it kept hidden in its heart. Opponents struck by these imbued fists will be shattered to their core.
flavor.59: Snaps at its foes with fangs cloaked in blazing flame. Despite its bulk, it deftly feints every which way, leading opponents on a deceptively merry chase as it all but dances around them.
flavor.62: Poliwrath is skilled at both swimming and martial arts. It uses its well-trained arms to dish out powerful punches.
flavor.186: The cry of a male is louder than that of a female. Male Politoed with deep, menacing voices find more popularity with the opposite gender.
flavor.65: The longer Alakazam lives, the larger and heavier its head becomes. Our tests have shown that the strength of its psychic powers correlates positively to the weight of its head.
flavor.68: In close combat, its four arms afford it offensive and defensive supremacy. In but a blink, this valiant Pokémon can overwhelm its foes with more than 1,000 blows from its fists.
flavor.71: Lures prey with the sweet aroma of honey. Swallowed whole, the prey is dissolved in a day, bones and all.
flavor.73: It has 80 tentacles, each with a venomous tip. These tentacles are also extendible, lengthening when Tentacruel attempts to catch prey. Use caution.
flavor.76: The rocklike shell is shed each year. The cast-off shell then crumbles, reverting to a mass of soil, which can be spread across fields to promote crop growth.
flavor.78: Fiery mane aglow, Rapidash darts like an arrow across the land. This prodigiously swift creature can traverse the vast region of Hisui in a day and a half.
flavor.80: Being bitten by a Shellder shocked this Pokémon into standing on two legs. If the Shellder lets go, it seems Slowbro will turn back into a Slowpoke.
flavor.199: Slowking can solve any problem presented to it, but no one can understand a thing Slowking says.
flavor.462: I theorize that a special magnetic field influenced this Pokémon, changing its molecular structure and causing it to evolve. It emits strange radio waves toward space from its antenna.
flavor.85: One of Doduo’s two heads splits to form a unique species. It runs close to 40 mph in prairies.
flavor.87: Its entire body is a snowy white. Unharmed by even intense cold, it swims powerfully in icy waters.
flavor.89: Smells so awful, it can cause fainting. Through degeneration of its nose, it lost its sense of smell.
flavor.91: Once it slams its shell shut, it is impossible to open, even by those with superior strength.
flavor.94: Possesses potential victims' shadows in an effort to steal away the victims' lives. If your shadow begins to laugh, you must take hold of a protective charm posthaste!
flavor.208: This Pokémon evolved through use of a strange item. Its body is coated with steel powder and notably hard—not even diamond can leave so much as a scratch.
flavor.97: Avoid eye contact if you come across one. It will try to put you to sleep by using its pendulum.
flavor.99: Its oversized claw is very powerful, but when it’s not in battle, the claw just gets in the way.
flavor.101: The tissue on the surface of its body is curiously similar in composition to an Apricorn. When irritated, this Pokémon lets loose an electric current equal to 20 lightning bolts.
flavor.103: When they work together, Exeggutor’s three heads can put out powerful psychic energy. Cloudy days make this Pokémon sluggish.
flavor.105: When this Pokémon evolved, the skull of its mother fused to it. Marowak’s temperament also turned vicious at the same time.
flavor.463: Its tongue can extend and contract freely, and it is capable of reaching lengths over 10 times Lickilicky's height. Beware of the saliva, as it contains corrosive elements.
flavor.110: It can’t suck in air quite as well as a Galarian Weezing, but the toxins it creates are more potent than those of its counterpart.
flavor.464: This Pokémon evolved through use of a curious item. Its rocklike hide is composed of a mysterious substance and can withstand a blow from a masterwork sword with nary a scratch.
flavor.465: Draped with long vines, it resembles a shrub in appearance. It swings bundles of vines as though they were arms, wrapping them around prey to ensnare them.
flavor.115: There are records of a lost human child being raised by a childless Kangaskhan.
flavor.230: Scales shed by this Pokémon have such a splendorous gleam to them that they’ve been given to royalty as gifts.
flavor.119: Using its horn, it bores holes in riverbed boulders, making nests to prevent its eggs from washing away.
flavor.121: Starmie swims by spinning its body at high speed. As this Pokémon cruises through the ocean, it absorbs tiny plankton.
flavor.212: Evolved by way of a curious item. The shell covering its body has been shown to be stronger than forged steel.
flavor.900: A violent creature that fells towering trees with its crude axes and shields itself with hard stone. If one should chance upon this Pokémon in the wilds, one's only recourse is to flee.
flavor.127: This Pokémon clamps its pincers down on its prey and then either splits the prey in half or flings it away.
flavor.128: The Tauros of the Galar region are volatile in nature, and they won’t allow people to ride on their backs.
flavor.130: I suspect this Pokémon to be the true identity of a dragon written of in ancient texts, which claimed that it razed an entire village with white-hot beams from its maw.
flavor.131: Crossing icy seas is no issue for this cold-resistant Pokémon. Its smooth skin is a little cool to the touch.
flavor.132: When it encounters another Ditto, it will move faster than normal to duplicate that opponent exactly.
flavor.134: Tests show that its cells closely resemble water molecules, which perhaps explains its ability to conceal its form while submerged. I believe the origins of mermaid folklore lie with this Pokémon.
flavor.135: Bristles its fur into sharp, needlelike points when enraged. One can hear electricity crackle in its breath when it exhales.
flavor.136: Flames burn within a saclike organ inside this Pokémon. When Flareon inhales, these flames grow in intensity, reaching a mighty 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit.
flavor.196: Wields an arcane power with which it can predict the weather and even people's thoughts. When bathed in sunshine, the scarlet orb on its brow glows and builds energy.
flavor.197: It is most active in the wee hours of the night, when moonlight bathes the land. Its large eyes can pierce the darkness and perceive prey with absolute clarity.
flavor.470: Cells similar to those of plants have been found in its fur. Its hard tail can fell a large tree with one stroke, and the tail's sharpness exceeds even that of a sword crafted by a master.
flavor.471: Glaceon is able to lower its body temperature very quickly. It freezes the atmosphere, creating diamond dust that glitters like gems while it flutters and dances around.
flavor.700: It emits a soothing aura from its ribbon-shaped organs. It wraps these appendages around quarrelers to instantly restore calm to the situation.
flavor.474: A curious item induced this evolution. The Pokémon's offensive capabilities have greatly increased, but the strangeness of its behavior has magnified in equal measure. This worries me.
flavor.139: Omastar’s sharp fangs could crush rock, but the Pokémon can attack only the prey that come within reach of its tentacles.
flavor.141: The cause behind the extinction of this species is unknown. Kabutops were aggressive Pokémon that inhabited warm seas.
flavor.142: Aerodactyl’s sawlike fangs can shred skin to tatters—even the skin of Steel-type Pokémon.
flavor.144: This Pokémon can control ice at will. Articuno is said to live in snowy mountains riddled with permafrost.
flavor.145: Zapdos is a legendary bird Pokémon. It’s said that when Zapdos rubs its feathers together, lightning will fall immediately after.
flavor.146: There are stories of this Pokémon using its radiant, flame-cloaked wings to light up paths for those lost in the mountains.
flavor.149: This Pokémon is known as the Sea Incarnate. Figureheads that resemble Dragonite decorate the bows of many ships.
flavor.150: Its DNA is almost the same as Mew’s. However, its size and disposition are vastly different.
flavor.151: When viewed through a microscope, this Pokémon’s short, fine, delicate hair can be seen.
flavor.154: The fragrance of Meganium’s flower soothes and calms emotions. In battle, this Pokémon gives off more of its becalming scent to blunt the foe’s fighting spirit.
flavor.157: Said to purify lost, forsaken souls with its flames and guide them to the afterlife. I believe its form has been influenced by the energy of the sacred mountain towering at Hisui's center.
flavor.160: Feraligatr intimidates its foes by opening its huge mouth. In battle, it will kick the ground hard with its thick and powerful hind legs to charge at the foe at an incredible speed.
flavor.162: Furret has a very slim build. When under attack, it can slickly squirm through narrow spaces and get away. In spite of its short limbs, this Pokémon is very nimble and fleet.
flavor.164: When it needs to think, it rotates its head 180 degrees to sharpen its intellectual power.
flavor.166: It flies through the night sky, sprinkling sparkly dust. According to some, if that dust sticks to you, good things will happen to you.
flavor.168: It spews threads from its mouth to catch its prey. When night falls, it leaves its web to go hunt aggressively.
flavor.171: This Pokémon flashes a bright light that blinds its prey. This creates an opening for it to deliver an electrical attack.
flavor.26: It can discharge bursts of electricity exceeding 100,000 volts— a single strike with that amount of power would incapacitate one of the Copperajah of my homeland.
flavor.36: Legend says that on clear, quiet nights, it listens for the voices of its kin living on the moon. I, too, often think of my homeland, so far away.
flavor.40: It’s proud of its fur, which is fine and delicate. In particular, the curl on its forehead has a texture that’s perfectly heavenly.
flavor.468: Scant few have ever sighted this Pokémon. After studying what literature remains, I am certain Togekiss will reveal itself when peace reigns in the land.
flavor.178: This odd Pokémon can see both the past and the future. It eyes the sun’s movement all day.
flavor.181: Its tail shines bright and strong. It has been prized since long ago as a beacon for sailors.
flavor.189: Jumpluff rides warm southern winds to cross the sea and fly to foreign lands. The Pokémon descends to the ground when it encounters cold air while it is floating.
flavor.424: To affirm their kinship, members of this species will form a ring by linking their newly doubled tails together. On rare occasions, humans have been accepted into such rings.
flavor.192: Sunflora converts solar energy into nutrition. It moves around actively in the daytime when it is warm. It stops moving as soon as the sun goes down for the night.
flavor.469: Extremely violent. When hunting, it wastes none of its energy, aiming only for prey's most vulnerable spots. Any who manage to tame this Pokémon must be of incredible bravery.
flavor.195: Its body is always slimy. It often bangs its head on the river bottom as it swims but seems not to care.
flavor.430: One cry from this Pokémon, and a murder of Murkrow come flying. At such times, one would think the curtain of night had fallen, plunging the world into jet-black darkness.
flavor.429: The incantations Mismagius chants can ward against misfortune, so a custom exists of inviting it into one's home. Incur the Pokémon's displeasure, however, and disaster will surely ensue.
flavor.201: It is hard to believe these strangely shaped Pokémon are truly living creatures. I've pointed out that the species' many forms resemble writing from other lands; no one will take me seriously.
flavor.981: The hardened head from the tail protects the head of the main body as Farigiraf whips its long neck around to headbutt enemies.
flavor.205: In the moment that it gulps down its prey, the inside of its shell is exposed, but to this day, no one has ever seen that sight.
flavor.982: It drives enemies out of its nest by sucking in enough air to fill its long, narrow lungs, then releasing the air in an intense blast.
flavor.472: It glides soundlessly on pitch-black wings and sinks sharp fangs into the throat of its prey. It takes on a look of satisfaction once it has entirely drained its prey of blood.
flavor.210: Although it’s popular with young people, Granbull is timid and sensitive, so it’s totally incompetent as a watchdog.
flavor.213: The berries stored in its vaselike shell eventually become a thick, pulpy juice.
flavor.214: This Pokémon has an unparalleled horn. Heracross itself demonstrates tremendous power—it's capable of throwing several people trained in the traditional arts of war at once.
flavor.461: This species corners prey as a pack, under the guidance of a leader. Weavile displays increased cunning, leading me to speculate that its evolution caused further brain development.
flavor.901: I believe it was Hisui's swampy terrain that gave Ursaluna its burly physique and newfound capacity to manipulate peat at will.
flavor.219: Magcargo’s body temperature is approximately 18,000 degrees Fahrenheit. Water is vaporized on contact. If this Pokémon is caught in the rain, the raindrops instantly turn into steam, cloaking the area in a thick fog.
flavor.473: This species reached its zenith during the period known as the ice age. I suspect that Hisui's frigid climate is in harmony with Mamoswine's constitution, thus awakening hidden potential.
flavor.224: While Octillery still shoots water from its mouth, the drastic anatomical difference between it and Remoraid meant that for a long time, no one believed the former evolved from the latter.
flavor.225: It has a generous habit of sharing its food with people and Pokémon, so it’s always scrounging around for more food.
flavor.227: People fashion swords from Skarmory’s shed feathers, so this Pokémon is a popular element in heraldic designs.
flavor.229: Identifiable by its eerie howls, people a long time ago thought it was the grim reaper and feared it.
flavor.232: If Donphan were to tackle with its hard body, even a house could be destroyed. Using its massive strength, the Pokémon helps clear rock and mud slides that block mountain trails.
flavor.899: The black orbs shine with an uncanny light when the Pokémon is erecting invisible barriers. The fur shed from its beard retains heat well and is a highly useful material for winter clothing.
flavor.235: It draws symbols with the fluid that oozes from the tip of its tail. Depending on the symbol, Smeargle fanatics will pay big money for them.
flavor.106: The legs freely contract and stretch. The stretchy legs allow it to hit a distant foe with a rising kick.
flavor.107: Its punches slice the air. However, it seems to need a short break after fighting for three minutes.
flavor.237: After doing a handstand to throw off the opponent’s timing, it presents its fancy kick moves.
flavor.124: The Jynx of Galar often have beautiful and delicate voices. Some of these Pokémon have even gathered a fan base.
flavor.466: Its evolution was induced by an unusual item, and its electrical output rises along with its heart rate. From its tails, it can unleash an electric current measuring 20,000 volts.
flavor.467: Use of a strange item caused this Pokémon to evolve. Fireballs launched from the ends of its tubelike arms are hot enough to melt an iron pot in an instant.
flavor.241: This Pokémon needs to be milked every day, or else it will fall ill. The flavor of Miltank milk changes with the seasons.
flavor.243: Raikou embodies the speed of lightning. The roars of this Pokémon send shock waves shuddering through the air and shake the ground as if lightning bolts had come crashing down.
flavor.244: Entei embodies the passion of magma. This Pokémon is thought to have been born in the eruption of a volcano. It sends up massive bursts of fire that utterly consume all that they touch.
flavor.245: Suicune embodies the compassion of a pure spring of water. It runs across the land with gracefulness. This Pokémon has the power to purify dirty water.
flavor.248: The quakes caused when it walks make even great mountains crumble and change the surrounding terrain.
flavor.249: Lugia’s wings pack devastating power—a light fluttering of its wings can blow apart regular houses. As a result, this Pokémon chooses to live out of sight deep under the sea.
flavor.250: Ho-Oh’s feathers glow in seven colors depending on the angle at which they are struck by light. These feathers are said to bring happiness to the bearers. This Pokémon is said to live at the foot of a rainbow.
flavor.251: This Pokémon traveled through time to come from the future. It bolsters grass and trees with its own strength, and it can heal wounds, too.
flavor.254: Sceptile has seeds growing on its back. They are said to be bursting with nutrients that revitalize trees. This Pokémon raises the trees in a forest with loving care.
flavor.257: Blaziken has incredibly strong legs—it can easily clear a 30-story building in one leap. This Pokémon’s blazing punches leave its foes scorched and blackened.
flavor.260: Swampert predicts storms by sensing subtle differences in the sounds of waves and tidal winds with its fins. If a storm is approaching, it piles up boulders to protect itself.
flavor.262: Mightyena travel and act as a pack in the wild. The memory of its life in the wild compels the Pokémon to obey only those Trainers that it recognizes to possess superior skill.
flavor.267: A colorful and incredibly beautiful but also greedy Pokémon. In an effort to keep its favorite food all to itself, it will chase away Combee as they try to gather nectar.
flavor.269: Tends to be drawn to bonfires on dark nights. Difficult to chase away from settlements because of the way it scatters highly toxic scales.
flavor.272: If it hears festive music, it begins moving in rhythm in order to amplify its power.
flavor.275: It lives quietly in the deep forest. It is said to create chilly winter winds with the fans it holds.
flavor.277: Swellow is very conscientious about the upkeep of its glossy wings. Once two Swellow are gathered, they diligently take care of cleaning each other’s wings.
flavor.279: Skimming the water’s surface, it dips its large bill in the sea, scoops up food and water, and carries it.
flavor.282: It will dedicate itself to defending a master it has come to adore. Its pure white dress, reminiscent of those worn by ladies of nobility, is the dress of one who is willing to risk their life.
flavor.475: The blades extending from its elbows are sharper than the finest swords. Its swordsmanship, albeit self-taught, is astonishingly impressive.
flavor.284: Its thin, winglike antennae are highly absorbent. It waits out rainy days in tree hollows.
flavor.286: The seeds ringing Breloom’s tail are made of hardened toxic spores. It is horrible to eat the seeds. Just taking a bite of this Pokémon’s seed will cause your stomach to rumble.
flavor.289: Wherever Slaking live, rings of over a yard in diameter appear in grassy fields. They are made by the Pokémon as it eats all the grass within reach while lying prone on the ground.
flavor.291: This Pokémon is so quick, it is said to be able to avoid any attack. It loves to feed on tree sap.
flavor.292: A strange Pokémon—it flies without moving its wings, has a hollow shell for a body, and does not breathe.
flavor.295: This Pokémon can do more than just shout. To communicate with others of its kind, it’ll emit all sorts of sounds from the holes in its body.
flavor.297: Hariyama that are big and fat aren’t necessarily strong. There are some small ones that move nimbly and use moves skillfully.
flavor.184: These Pokémon create air-filled bubbles. When Azurill play in rivers, Azumarill will cover them with these bubbles.
flavor.476: It is able to emit powerful magnetism, allowing it control over the iron sand that forms its luscious mustache. Using this iron sand, Probopass forms hard stones with which it smites its prey.
flavor.301: Delcatty sleeps anywhere it wants without keeping a permanent nest. If other Pokémon approach it as it sleeps, this Pokémon will never fight—it will just move away somewhere else.
flavor.302: It feeds on gemstone crystals. In darkness, its eyes sparkle with the glitter of jewels.
flavor.303: It chomps with its gaping mouth. Its huge jaws are actually steel horns that have been transformed.
flavor.306: Long ago, there was a king who wore a helmet meant to resemble the head of an Aggron. He was trying to channel the Pokémon’s strength.
flavor.308: Through the power of meditation, Medicham developed its sixth sense. It gained the ability to use psychokinetic powers. This Pokémon is known to meditate for a whole month without eating.
flavor.310: It rarely appears before people. It is said to nest where lightning has fallen.
flavor.311: When Plusle is cheering on its partner, it flashes with electric sparks from all over its body. If its partner loses, this Pokémon cries loudly.
flavor.312: Minun loves to cheer on its partner in battle. It gives off sparks from its body while it is doing so. If its partner is in trouble, this Pokémon gives off increasing amounts of sparks.
flavor.313: Volbeat’s tail glows like a lightbulb. With other Volbeat, it uses its tail to draw geometric shapes in the night sky. This Pokémon loves the sweet aroma given off by Illumise.
flavor.314: Illumise leads a flight of illuminated Volbeat to draw signs in the night sky. This Pokémon is said to earn greater respect from its peers by composing more complex designs in the sky.
flavor.317: Swalot has no teeth, so what it eats, it swallows whole, no matter what. Its cavernous mouth yawns widely. An automobile tire could easily fit inside this Pokémon’s mouth.
flavor.319: This Pokémon is known as the Bully of the Sea. Any ship entering the waters Sharpedo calls home will be attacked—no exceptions.
flavor.321: Its immense size is the reason for its popularity. Wailord watching is a favorite sightseeing activity in various parts of the world.
flavor.323: The humps on Camerupt’s back are formed by a transformation of its bones. They sometimes blast out molten magma. This Pokémon apparently erupts often when it is enraged.
flavor.324: You find abandoned coal mines full of them. They dig tirelessly in search of coal.
flavor.326: Grumpig uses the black pearls on its body to wield its fantastic powers. When it is doing so, it dances bizarrely. This Pokémon’s black pearls are valuable as works of art.
flavor.327: Each Spinda’s spot pattern is different. With its stumbling movements, it evades opponents’ attacks brilliantly!
flavor.330: It is nicknamed the Desert Spirit because the flapping of its wings sounds like a woman singing.
flavor.332: If a traveler is going through a desert in the thick of night, Cacturne will follow in a ragtag group. The Pokémon are biding their time, waiting for the traveler to tire and become incapable of moving.
flavor.334: This Pokémon has a kind disposition, but if it’s provoked, it will threaten opponents with shrill cries before attacking them without mercy.
flavor.335: Zangoose usually stays on all fours, but when angered, it gets up on its hind legs and extends its claws. This Pokémon shares a bitter rivalry with Seviper that dates back over generations.
flavor.336: Seviper’s swordlike tail serves two purposes—it slashes foes and douses them with secreted poison. This Pokémon will not give up its long-running blood feud with Zangoose.
flavor.337: It was discovered at the site of a meteor strike 40 years ago. Its stare can lull its foes to sleep.
flavor.338: Solar energy is the source of its power, so it is strong during the daytime. When it spins, its body shines.
flavor.340: Strikes its caudal fin against the swamp bed to shake the ground and startle its prey. It will then swallow the fleeing prey whole. People mistook this behavior as the cause of earthquakes.
flavor.342: A brutish Pokémon that loves to battle. It will crash itself into any foe that approaches its nest.
flavor.344: It appears to have been born from clay dolls made by ancient people. It uses telekinesis to float and move.
flavor.346: Once Cradily catches prey in its tentacles, it digests them whole and absorbs their nutrients.
flavor.348: Though it lives on land, it’s also a good swimmer. It dives into the ocean in search of prey, using its sharp claws to take down its quarry.
flavor.350: It’s said that a glimpse of a Milotic and its beauty will calm any hostile emotions you’re feeling.
flavor.351: Its form changes depending on the weather. The rougher conditions get, the rougher Castform’s disposition!
flavor.352: Its color changes for concealment and also when its mood or health changes. The darker the color, the healthier it is.
flavor.354: Resentment at being cast off made it spring into being. Some say that treating it well will satisfy it, and it will once more become a stuffed toy.
flavor.477: Comes to those whose lives have come to an end and escorts their souls to the afterlife. Known to mistakenly take the souls of those who yet have life left in them, albeit rarely.
flavor.357: Bunches of delicious fruit grow around its neck. In warm areas, many ranches raise Tropius.
flavor.359: Because of this Pokémon’s ability to detect danger, people mistook Absol as a bringer of doom.
flavor.202: To keep its pitch-black tail hidden, it lives quietly in the darkness. It is never first to attack.
flavor.362: It covers its body with an armor of ice harder than steel. Uses its breath to freeze prey, which it then devours as if they were frozen desserts.
flavor.478: A Pokémon inhabited by the soul of a woman who died bearing a grudge in the snowy mountains. Legends of Froslass placing deathly curses on misbehaving men send shivers down my spine.
flavor.365: Its thick tusks are strong enough to shatter drift ice. They have been known to break, but they will grow back by the next year. The Hisui region is well known for these broken tusks.
flavor.367: Deep seas are their habitat. According to tradition, when Huntail wash up onshore, something unfortunate will happen.
flavor.368: It sucks bodily fluids out of its prey. The leftover meat sinks to the seafloor, where it becomes food for other Pokémon.
flavor.369: This Pokémon was discovered during deep-sea exploration. Its appearance hasn’t changed in 100,000,000 years, so it’s called a living fossil.
flavor.370: Luvdisc makes its home in coral reefs in warm seas. It especially likes sleeping in the space between Corsola’s branches.
flavor.373: While basking in the joy of flight generally keeps this Pokémon in high spirits, Salamence turns into an uncontrollable menace if something angers it.
flavor.376: Metagross is the result of the fusion of two Metang. This Pokémon defeats its opponents through use of its supercomputer-level brain.
flavor.377: Cutting-edge technology was used to study the internals of this Pokémon’s rock body, but nothing was found—not even a brain or a heart.
flavor.378: This Pokémon’s body is made of solid ice. It’s said that Regice was born beneath thick ice in the ice age.
flavor.379: It’s rumored that this Pokémon was born deep underground in the planet’s mantle and that it emerged onto the surface 10,000 years ago.
flavor.380: Latias is highly intelligent and capable of understanding human speech. It is covered with a glass-like down. The Pokémon enfolds its body with its down and refracts light to alter its appearance.
flavor.381: Latios will only open its heart to a Trainer with a compassionate spirit. This Pokémon can fly faster than a jet plane by folding its forelegs to minimize air resistance.
flavor.382: Kyogre is said to be the personification of the sea itself. Legends tell of its many clashes against Groudon, as each sought to gain the power of nature.
flavor.383: Through Primal Reversion and with nature’s full power, it will take back its true form. It can cause magma to erupt and expand the landmass of the world.
flavor.384: It flies forever through the ozone layer, consuming meteoroids for sustenance. The many meteoroids in its body provide the energy it needs to Mega Evolve.
flavor.385: It’s believed that when this Pokémon wakes from its 1,000-year slumber, it will grant any wishes written on the notes attached to its head.
flavor.386: Deoxys emerged from a virus that came from space. It is highly intelligent and wields psychokinetic powers. This Pokémon shoots lasers from the crystalline organ on its chest.
flavor.389: This remarkable, large-bodied Pokémon would serve beautifully as borrowed scenery for a garden, and its strength is peerless. Torterra roams the wilderness in search of clean water.
flavor.392: A tall, hardy Pokémon with a dazzling appearance. It shrouds itself in flame and battles as if engaged in dance—truly a sight to behold.
flavor.395: Since ancient times, it has been revered by the people of Hisui, who call it the Master of the Waves. Its wings are a match for even master-crafted blades.

flavor.812: The one with the best drumming techniques becomes the boss of the troop. It has a gentle disposition and values harmony among its group.
flavor.815: It’s skilled at both offense and defense, and it gets pumped up when cheered on. But if it starts showboating, it could put itself in a tough spot.
flavor.818: Its nictitating membranes let it pick out foes’ weak points so it can precisely blast them with water that shoots from its fingertips at Mach 3.
flavor.820: Common throughout the Galar region, this Pokémon has strong teeth and can chew through the toughest of berry shells.
flavor.823: With their great intellect and flying skills, these Pokémon very successfully act as the Galar region’s airborne taxi service.
flavor.826: It emits psychic energy to observe and study what’s around it—and what’s around it can include things over six miles away.
flavor.828: With a lithe body and sharp claws, it goes around stealing food and eggs. Boltund is its natural enemy.
flavor.830: The cotton on the head of this Pokémon can be spun into a glossy, gorgeous yarn—a Galar regional specialty.
flavor.832: Its majestic horns are meant only to impress the opposite gender. They never see use in battle.
flavor.834: This Pokémon rapidly extends its retractable neck to sink its sharp fangs into distant enemies and take them down.
flavor.836: It sends electricity through its legs to boost their strength. Running at top speed, it easily breaks 50 mph.
flavor.839: While it’s engaged in battle, its mountain of coal will burn bright red, sending off sparks that scorch the surrounding area.
flavor.841: It flies on wings of apple skin and spits a powerful acid. It can also change its shape into that of an apple.
flavor.842: Its body is covered in sweet nectar, and the skin on its back is especially yummy. Children used to have it as a snack.
flavor.1019: These capricious syrpents have banded together. On the rare occasion that their moods align, their true power is unleashed.
flavor.844: Its unique style of coiling allows it to blast sand out of its sand sac more efficiently.
flavor.845: This hungry Pokémon swallows Arrokuda whole. Occasionally, it makes a mistake and tries to swallow a Pokémon other than its preferred prey.
flavor.847: It spins its tail fins to propel itself, surging forward at speeds of over 100 knots before ramming prey and spearing into them.
flavor.849: This short-tempered and aggressive Pokémon chugs stagnant water to absorb any toxins it might contain.
flavor.851: While its burning body is already dangerous on its own, this excessively hostile Pokémon also has large and very sharp fangs.
flavor.853: Searching for an opponent to test its skills against, it emerges onto land. Once the battle is over, it returns to the sea.
flavor.855: Leaving leftover black tea unattended is asking for this Pokémon to come along and pour itself into it, turning the tea into a new Polteageist.
flavor.858: If you’re too loud around it, you risk being torn apart by the claws on its tentacle. This Pokémon is also known as the Forest Witch.
flavor.861: Its hairs work like muscle fibers. When its hairs unfurl, they latch on to opponents, ensnaring them as tentacles would.
flavor.869: When Alcremie is content, the cream it secretes from its hands becomes sweeter and richer.
flavor.870: The six of them work together as one Pokémon. Teamwork is also their battle strategy, and they constantly change their formation as they fight.
flavor.871: It stores electricity in each spine. Even if one gets broken off, it still continues to emit electricity for at least three hours.
flavor.873: It shows no mercy to any who desecrate fields and mountains. It will fly around on its icy wings, causing a blizzard to chase offenders away.
flavor.874: Once a year, on a specific date and at a specific time, they gather out of nowhere and form up in a circle.
flavor.875: This Pokémon keeps its heat-sensitive head cool with ice. It fishes for its food, dangling its single hair into the sea to lure in prey.
flavor.876: Through its horns, it can pick up on the emotions of creatures around it. Positive emotions are the source of its strength.
flavor.877: It carries electrically roasted seeds with it as if they’re precious treasures. No matter how much it eats, it always gets hungry again in short order.
flavor.879: These Pokémon live in herds. Their trunks have incredible grip strength, strong enough to crush giant rocks into powder.
flavor.880: The powerful muscles in its tail generate its electricity. Compared to its lower body, its upper half is entirely too small.
flavor.881: This Pokémon lived on prehistoric seashores and was able to preserve food with the ice on its body. It went extinct because it moved so slowly.
flavor.882: Its mighty legs are capable of running at speeds exceeding 40 mph, but this Pokémon can’t breathe unless it’s underwater.
flavor.883: The skin on its face is impervious to attack, but breathing difficulties made this Pokémon go extinct anyway.
flavor.1018: It digs holes on mountains, searching for food. It’s so durable that being caught in a cave-in won’t faze it.
flavor.887: Apparently the Dreepy inside Dragapult’s horns eagerly look forward to being launched out at Mach speeds.
flavor.888: This Pokémon has slumbered for many years. Some say it’s Zamazenta’s elder sister—others say the two Pokémon are rivals.
flavor.889: This Pokémon slept for aeons while in the form of a statue. It was asleep for so long, people forgot that it ever existed.
flavor.890: It was inside a meteorite that fell 20,000 years ago. There seems to be a connection between this Pokémon and the Dynamax phenomenon.
flavor.892: Inhabiting the mountains of a distant region, this Pokémon races across sheer cliffs, training its legs and refining its moves.
flavor.893: Once the vines on Zarude’s body tear off, they become nutrients in the soil. This helps the plants of the forest grow.
flavor.894: Its entire body is made up of a single organ that generates electrical energy. Regieleki is capable of creating all Galar’s electricity.
flavor.895: Its body is composed of crystallized dragon energy. Regidrago is said to have the powers of every dragon Pokémon.
flavor.896: Glastrier has tremendous physical strength, and the mask of ice covering its face is 100 times harder than diamond.
flavor.897: As it dashes through the night, Spectrier absorbs the life-force of sleeping creatures. It craves silence and solitude.
flavor.898: Calyrex is known in legend as a king that ruled over Galar in ancient times. It has the power to cause hearts to mend and plants to spring forth.
flavor.905: When it flies to this land from across the sea, the bitter winter comes to an end. According to legend, this Pokémon's love gives rise to the budding of fresh life across Hisui.
flavor.908: With skillful misdirection, it rigs foes with pollen-packed flower bombs. Meowscarada sets off the bombs before its foes realize what’s going on.
flavor.911: Skeledirge’s gentle singing soothes the souls of all that hear it. It burns its enemies to a crisp with flames of over 5,400 degrees Fahrenheit.
flavor.914: Dancing in ways that evoke far-away places, this Pokémon mesmerizes all that see it. Flourishes of its decorative water feathers slice into its foes.
flavor.916: It entrances female Pokémon with the sweet, alluring scent that wafts from all over its body.
flavor.918: Spidops covers its territory in tough, sticky threads to set up traps for intruders.
flavor.920: It uses its normally folded third set of legs when in Showdown Mode. This places a huge burden on its body, so it can’t stay in this mode for long.
flavor.923: Pawmot’s fluffy fur acts as a battery. It can store the same amount of electricity as an electric car.
flavor.925: The larger pair protects the little ones during battles. When facing strong opponents, the whole group will join the fight.
flavor.927: The surface of this Pokémon’s skin hardens when exposed to intense heat, and its body has an appetizing aroma.
flavor.930: This Pokémon drives back enemies by launching its rich, aromatic oil at them with enough force to smash a boulder.
flavor.931: Green-feathered flocks hold the most sway. When they’re out searching for food in the mornings and evenings, it gets very noisy.
flavor.934: Many Pokémon gather around Garganacl, hoping to lick at its mineral-rich salt.
flavor.936: This Pokémon clads itself in armor that has been fortified by psychic and fire energy, and it shoots blazing fireballs.
flavor.937: An old set of armor steeped in grudges caused this Pokémon’s evolution. Ceruledge cuts its enemies to pieces without mercy.
flavor.939: What appear to be eyeballs are actually organs for discharging the electricity generated by Bellibolt’s belly-button dynamo.
flavor.941: It uses its throat sac to store electricity generated by its wings. There’s hardly any oil in its feathers, so it is a poor swimmer.
flavor.943: Mabosstiff loves playing with children. Though usually gentle, it takes on an intimidating look when protecting its family.
flavor.945: Each Grafaiai paints its own individual pattern, and it will paint that same pattern over and over again throughout its life.
flavor.947: Brambleghast wanders around arid regions. On rare occasions, mass outbreaks of these Pokémon will bury an entire town.
flavor.949: It coils its 10 tentacles around prey and sucks out their nutrients, causing the prey pain. The folds along the rim of its head are a popular delicacy.
flavor.950: This Pokémon lives on sheer cliffs. It sidesteps opponents’ attacks, then lunges for their weak spots with its claws.
flavor.952: The green head has turned vicious due to the spicy chemicals stimulating its brain. Once it goes on a rampage, there is no stopping it.
flavor.954: An infant sleeps inside the ball. Rabsca rolls the ball soothingly with its legs to ensure the infant sleeps comfortably.
flavor.956: It emits psychic power from the gaps between its multicolored frills and sprints at speeds greater than 120 mph.
flavor.959: The hammer tops 220 pounds, yet it gets swung around easily by Tinkaton as it steals whatever it pleases and carries its plunder back home.
flavor.961: A variety of fish Pokémon, Wugtrio was once considered to be a regional form of Dugtrio.
flavor.962: Bombirdier uses the apron on its chest to bundle up food, which it carries back to its nest. It enjoys dropping things that make loud noises.
flavor.964: Its physical capabilities are no different than a Finizen’s, but when its allies are in danger, it transforms and powers itself up.
flavor.966: Revavroom viciously threatens others with the sound of its exhaust. It sticks its tongue out from its cylindrical mouth and sprays toxic fluids.
flavor.967: It can sprint at over 70 mph while carrying a human. The rider’s body heat warms Cyclizar’s back and lifts the Pokémon’s spirit.
flavor.968: This Pokémon lives in arid deserts. It maintains its metal body by consuming iron from the soil.
flavor.970: Glimmora’s petals are made of crystallized poison energy. It has recently become evident that these petals resemble Tera Jewels.
flavor.972: A lovingly mourned Pokémon was reborn as Houndstone. It doesn’t like anyone touching the protuberance atop its head.
flavor.973: Thanks to a behavior of theirs known as “synchronizing,” an entire flock of these Pokémon can attack simultaneously in perfect harmony.
flavor.975: Ice energy builds up in the horn on its upper jaw, causing the horn to reach cryogenic temperatures that freeze its surroundings.
flavor.976: Veluza has excellent regenerative capabilities. It sheds spare flesh from its body to boost its agility, then charges at its prey.
flavor.977: It treats Tatsugiri like its boss and follows it loyally. Though powerful, Dondozo is apparently not very smart.
flavor.978: Tatsugiri is an extremely cunning Pokémon. It feigns weakness to lure in prey, then orders its partner to attack.
flavor.984: This creature resembles a mysterious Pokémon that, according to a paranormal magazine, has lived since ancient times.
flavor.985: It resembles a mysterious Pokémon described in a paranormal magazine as a Jigglypuff from one billion years ago.
flavor.986: It bears a slight resemblance to a Pokémon described in a dubious magazine as a cross between a dinosaur and a mushroom.
flavor.987: It has similar features to a ghostly pterosaur that was covered in a paranormal magazine, but the two have little else in common.
flavor.988: This Pokémon somewhat resembles an ancient form of Volcarona that was introduced in a dubious magazine.
flavor.989: It slightly resembles a Magneton that lived for 10,000 years and was featured in an article in a paranormal magazine.
flavor.990: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. It resembles a mysterious object described in an old expedition journal.
flavor.991: It resembles a mysterious object mentioned in an old book. There are only two reported sightings of this Pokémon.
flavor.992: This Pokémon shares many similarities with Iron Hands, an object mentioned in a certain expedition journal.
flavor.993: It’s possible that Iron Jugulis, an object described in an old book, may actually be this Pokémon.
flavor.994: No records exist of this species being caught. Data is lacking, but the Pokémon’s traits match up with an object described in an old book.
flavor.995: Some of its notable features match those of an object named within a certain expedition journal as Iron Thorns.
flavor.998: It launches itself into battle by flipping upside down and spewing frigid air from its mouth. It finishes opponents off with its dorsal blade.
flavor.1000: It has a sturdy body made up of stacked coins. Gholdengo overwhelms its enemies by firing coin after coin at them in quick succession.
flavor.1001: It drains the life-force from vegetation, causing nearby forests to instantly wither and fields to turn barren.
flavor.1002: The hatred of those who perished by the sword long ago has clad itself in snow and become a Pokémon.
flavor.1003: It slowly brings its exceedingly heavy head down upon the ground, splitting the earth open with huge fissures that run over 160 feet deep.
flavor.1004: The envy accumulated within curved beads that sparked multiple conflicts has clad itself in fire and become a Pokémon.
flavor.1005: According to an article in a dubious magazine, this Pokémon has some connection to a phenomenon that occurs in a certain region.
flavor.1006: It’s possible that this is the object listed as Iron Valiant in a certain expedition journal.
flavor.1007: This Pokémon resembles Cyclizar, but it is far burlier and more ferocious. Nothing is known about its ecology or other features.
flavor.1008: This seems to be the Iron Serpent mentioned in an old book. The Iron Serpent is said to have turned the land to ash with its lightning.
flavor.1009: It resembles an illustration published in a paranormal magazine, said to be a depiction of a super-ancient Suicune.
flavor.1010: According to the few eyewitness accounts that exist, it used its shining blades to julienne large trees and boulders.
flavor.1013: It prefers cool, dark places, such as the back of a shelf or the space beneath a home's floorboards. It wanders in search of prey after sunset.
flavor.1014: Okidogi is a ruffian with a short temper. It can pulverize anything by swinging around the chain on its neck.
flavor.1015: Munkidori keeps itself somewhere safe while it toys with its foes, using psychokinesis to induce intense dizziness.
flavor.1016: Fezandipiti beats its glossy wings to scatter pheromones that captivate people and Pokémon.
flavor.1017: This mischief-loving Pokémon is full of curiosity. It battles by drawing out the type-based energy contained within its masks.
flavor.1020: It resembles an eerie Pokémon once shown in a paranormal magazine. That Pokémon was said to be an Entei regenerated from a fossil.
flavor.1021: It bears resemblance to a Pokémon that became a hot topic for a short while after a paranormal magazine touted it as Raikou's ancestor.
flavor.1022: It was named after a mysterious object recorded in an old book. Its body seems to be metallic.
flavor.1023: There was supposedly an incident in which it launched shining blades to cut everything around it to pieces. Little else is known about it.
flavor.1024: It’s thought that this Pokémon lived in ancient Paldea until it got caught in seismic shifts and went extinct.
flavor.1025: Its peach-shaped shell serves as storage for a potent poison. It makes poisonous mochi and serves them to people and Pokémon.
flavor.863: After many battles, it evolved dangerous claws that come together to form daggers when extended.
flavor.865: After deflecting attacks with its hard leaf shield, it strikes back with its sharp leek stalk. The leek stalk is both weapon and food.
flavor.866: Its amusing movements make it very popular. It releases its psychic power from the pattern on its belly.
flavor.864: Be cautious of the ectoplasmic body surrounding its soul. You’ll become stiff as stone if you touch it.
flavor.862: It evolved after experiencing numerous fights. While crossing its arms, it lets out a shout that would make any opponent flinch.
flavor.867: Never touch its shadowlike body, or you’ll be shown the horrific memories behind the picture carved into it.
flavor.904: Its lancelike spikes and savage temperament have earned it the nickname ”sea fiend.” It slurps up poison to nourish itself.
flavor.903: Because of Sneasler's virulent poison and daunting physical prowess, no other species could hope to best it on the frozen highlands. Preferring solitude, this species does not form packs.
flavor.902: Clads itself in the souls of comrades that perished before fulfilling their goals of journeying upstream. No other species throughout all Hisui's rivers is Basculegion's equal.
flavor.980: It lives at the bottom of ponds and swamps. It will carry Wooper on its back and ferry them across water from one shore to the other.

lineFlavor.10091-10092: It forms a group of Rattata, which it assumes command of. Each group has its own territory, and disputes over food happen often.
lineFlavor.172-25-10100: This Pokémon rides on its tail while it uses its psychic powers to levitate. It attacks with star-shaped thunderbolts.
lineFlavor.10101-10102: Many people climb snowy mountains, hoping to see the icy spikes of these Pokémon glistening in the light of dawn.
lineFlavor.10103-10104: It lives on mountains perpetually covered in snow and is revered as a deity incarnate. It appears draped in a blizzard.
lineFlavor.10105-10106: The three of them get along very well. Through their formidable teamwork, they defeat powerful opponents.
lineFlavor.10107-10108: The round face of Alolan Persian is considered to be a symbol of prosperity in the Alola region, so these Pokémon are very well cared for.
lineFlavor.10109-10110-10111: Because it can’t fire boulders at a rapid pace, it’s been known to seize nearby Geodude and fire them from its back.
lineFlavor.10112-10113: The garbage it eats causes continuous chemical changes in its body, which produce its exceedingly vivid coloration.
lineFlavor.102-10114: Blazing sunlight has brought out the true form and powers of this Pokémon.
lineFlavor.104-10115: This Pokémon sets the bone it holds on fire and dances through the night as a way to mourn its fallen allies.
lineFlavor.10162-10163: Brave and prideful, this Pokémon dashes airily through the forest, its steps aided by the psychic power stored in the fur on its fetlocks.
lineFlavor.10164-10165: A Shellder bite set off a chemical reaction with the spices inside Slowbro's body, causing Slowbro to become a Poison-type Pokémon.
lineFlavor.10164-10172: While chanting strange spells, this Pokémon combines its internal toxins with what it's eaten, creating strange potions.
lineFlavor.109-10167: This Pokémon consumes particles that contaminate the air. Instead of leaving droppings, it expels clean air.
lineFlavor.10176-10177: On days when blizzards blow through, it comes down to where people live. It stashes food in the snowball on its head, taking it home for later.
lineFlavor.10180: Its conspicuous lips lure prey in as it lies in wait in the mud. When prey gets close, Stunfisk clamps its jagged steel fins down on them.
lineFlavor.10250: This kind of Tauros, known as the Combat Breed, is distinguished by its thick, powerful muscles and its fierce disposition.
lineFlavor.10251: When heated by fire energy, its horns can get hotter than 1,800 degrees Fahrenheit. Those gored by them will suffer both wounds and burns.
lineFlavor.10252: This Pokémon blasts water from holes on the tips of its horns—the high-pressure jets pierce right through Tauros's enemies.
lineFlavor.10169: Its feather-like blades are composed of psychic energy and can shear through thick iron sheets as if they were paper.
lineFlavor.10170: One kick from its powerful legs will pulverize a dump truck. Supposedly, this Pokémon runs through the mountains at over 180 mph.
lineFlavor.10171: This Pokémon's sinister, flame-like aura will consume the spirit of any creature it hits. Victims become burned-out shadows of themselves.
